title: Dual evaluation and scalar endomorphisms of a rank-one projective module
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $L$ a direct summand of a finite free $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. Assume that for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ the localized module $L_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] is free of rank one, meaning isomorphic to $R_{\mathfrak p}$ as an $R_{\mathfrak p}$-module. Put $L^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_R(L,R)$, and use ordinary tensor products [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Then the evaluation map $e_L:L^\vee\otimes_R L\to R$, $\lambda\otimes l\mapsto\lambda(l)$, is an isomorphism. The scalar map $c_L:R\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(L,L)$, $r\mapsto(l\mapsto rl)$, is an $R$-linear isomorphism. In particular $L^\vee$ is a tensor inverse of $L$ under ordinary tensor symmetry.

source.place: Tag 0B8I (lemma-invertible), equivalence (1)--(3) and its evaluation proof; Tag 0FJ9 (section-determinants), paragraph preceding remark-determinant-as-socle, the identification R = Hom_R(L,L) for an invertible module.

proof.text: Choose splitting maps $i:L\to R^n$, $s:R^n\to L$ with $si=1$ from the direct-summand hypothesis [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. For the standard vectors $e_j$ put $x_j=s(e_j)$ and $\lambda_j=\operatorname{pr}_j i\in L^\vee$. Expanding $i(x)$ in coordinates gives $x=\sum_j\lambda_j(x)x_j$ for every $x\in L$. Applying any $\lambda\in L^\vee$ gives $\lambda=\sum_j\lambda(x_j)\lambda_j$. Both are finite sums, including when $n=0$.

source.place: Tag 0B8I, lemma-invertible, evaluation argument; details supplied by a dual basis and Algebra Tag 00HN (lemma-characterize-zero-local (1)).

proof.text: For each prime $\mathfrak p$, extend a functional $\lambda:L\to R$ to $\lambda_{\mathfrak p}:L_{\mathfrak p}\to R_{\mathfrak p}$ by $\lambda_{\mathfrak p}(x/a)=\lambda(x)/a$. This is well-defined: $u(bx-ay)=0$ implies $u(b\lambda(x)-a\lambda(y))=0$, exactly the fraction relation [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]; the same formula verifies $R_{\mathfrak p}$-linearity. Choose a generator $v$ of $L_{\mathfrak p}\cong R_{\mathfrak p}$. Writing $x/1=av$, $y/1=bv$ shows $(\lambda(x)y-\lambda(y)x)/1=0$. Apply each coordinate functional $\lambda_j$ to this equality: the scalar $\lambda_j(\lambda(x)y-\lambda(y)x)$ vanishes in every $R_{\mathfrak p}$, hence is zero by [lem-weil-pbc-prime-localizations-jointly-injective]. The expansion in step 1 then proves the global identity $\lambda(x)y=\lambda(y)x$.

source.place: Tag 0B8I, lemma-invertible, evaluation argument; details supplied by a dual basis and Algebra Tag 00HN (lemma-characterize-zero-local (1)).

proof.text: Put $t=\sum_j\lambda_j(x_j)$. At a prime choose the generator $v$ as in step 2, and write $x_j/1=a_jv$, $b_j=(\lambda_j)_{\mathfrak p}(v)$. The localized expansion of step 1, applied to $v$, says $v=(\sum_j b_ja_j)v$. (It holds on fractions by dividing the expansion for their numerators.) Since $v$ is a free generator, $\sum_j b_ja_j=1$. Thus $t/1=\sum_j a_jb_j=1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-prime-localizations-jointly-injective], $t=1$ in $R$. This argument also covers the zero ring: the same injectivity assertion with an empty product forces the scalar equality.

source.place: Tag 0B8I, lemma-invertible, evaluation argument; details supplied by a dual basis and Algebra Tag 00HN (lemma-characterize-zero-local (1)).

proof.text:
By the tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], the bilinear pairing $(\lambda,x)\mapsto\lambda(x)$ induces the stated $e_L$. Put $\xi=\sum_j\lambda_j\otimes x_j$ and define $a:R\to L^\vee\otimes_R L$ by $a(r)=r\xi$. Step 3 gives $e_La(r)=r$. For a pure tensor, step 2 and tensor balancing give
$$a e_L(\lambda\otimes x)=\sum_j\lambda_j\otimes\lambda(x)x_j=\sum_j\lambda_j\otimes\lambda(x_j)x=\Bigl(\sum_j\lambda(x_j)\lambda_j\Bigr)\otimes x=\lambda\otimes x.$$
Pure tensors generate, so $a e_L=1$ and $e_L$ is an isomorphism. The swap $x\otimes\lambda\mapsto\lambda\otimes x$ is well-defined by bilinearity and is its own inverse; composing with $e_L$ gives the other evaluation isomorphism and the asserted tensor inverse.

source.place: Tag 0B8I, lemma-invertible, evaluation argument; details supplied by a dual basis and Algebra Tag 00HN (lemma-characterize-zero-local (1)).

proof.text:
For $f\in\operatorname{Hom}_R(L,L)$ define $h(f)=\sum_j\lambda_j(f(x_j))\in R$. This is $R$-linear, and $c_L$ is $R$-linear directly from its scalar formula. Steps 1 and 2 give
$$f(x)=\sum_j\lambda_j(x)f(x_j)=\sum_j\lambda_j(f(x_j))x=h(f)x,$$
so $c_Lh(f)=f$. Step 3 gives $h(c_L(r))=r\sum_j\lambda_j(x_j)=r$. Thus $h$ and $c_L$ are inverse $R$-linear maps. No choice of a global generator of $L$ has been made.
